Title: Repository, tooling and CI
User story: As a builder, I want a monorepo with the API app, migrations, lint, type checks and tests running in CI, so that every story ships tested and nothing merges red.
Acceptance criteria:
- `make test`, `make lint` (ruff) and `make typecheck` (mypy, strict on `detent/domain`) pass locally and in GitHub Actions on every push
- CI starts a Postgres 16 service and runs Alembic migrations before tests
- `.env.example` lists every setting; a secret scanner runs as a pre-commit hook and in CI
- The README explains setup in under 10 commands

Title: Settings and test-network guard
User story: As a builder, I want the app to refuse to start with any mainnet chain ID or live credentials, so that the prototype can never move real money.
Acceptance criteria:
- Given a configured chain ID outside {84532 Base Sepolia, 11155111 Ethereum Sepolia, 31337 local}, when the app or worker starts, then it exits with a clear error
- Given an API key prefix `sk_live_`, when any request uses it, then it is rejected with 403 `live_mode_unavailable`
- Settings load via pydantic-settings; no setting is read from os.environ elsewhere

Title: Baseline schema and ID conventions
User story: As a builder, I want the core tables, enums and constraints from spec/02-domain-model.md as the first migration, so that invariants are enforced by the database, not just by code.
Acceptance criteria:
- IDs are prefixed UUIDv7 strings (`pay_`, `att_`, `dec_`, `exc_`, `dep_`, `evt_`, `org_`)
- Money is stored as integer minor units plus an ISO currency code; no floats anywhere in money paths
- Every table carries `org_id`; every query in the repository layer filters by it
- Partial unique indexes from the domain model exist (one in-flight attempt, one confirmed attempt per payment)

Title: Demo login and acting-user switcher
User story: As a demo viewer, I want one demo password and a switcher to act as the payments lead, compliance lead, reviewer, backup owner or on-call engineer, so that the demo shows who is allowed to do what without building full auth.
Acceptance criteria:
- One shared password protects the console; after login the viewer picks an acting user
- Every write records the acting user ID and role in the audit log
- Role checks run on the server; hiding a button is never the only control

Title: Controllable clock
User story: As a demo viewer, I want to fast-forward time in demo mode, so that deadlines, overdue escalations and UNKNOWN resolution can be shown in minutes.
Acceptance criteria:
- All code reads time from a Clock service; a lint rule or test fails on direct `datetime.now()` in `detent/`
- In demo mode the console can advance the clock by 15 min, 1 h or 1 day; outside demo mode the control is absent
- Tests use a frozen clock

Title: Background worker and job loop
User story: As a builder, I want one worker process running scheduled and queued jobs from Postgres, so that UNKNOWN resolution, deadline sweeps, chain watching and webhook delivery survive restarts.
Acceptance criteria:
- Jobs are claimed with `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`; each job is idempotent
- Killing the worker mid-job and restarting it never duplicates a side effect (tested)
- Job runs, failures and durations are logged with the payment ID where relevant

Title: Deploy to an EU region
User story: As a founder, I want the web app and worker deployed in an EU region with Postgres in an EU region, so that the demo is reachable and data residency is truthful.
Acceptance criteria:
- Web service and worker deploy from main; database is Neon in an EU region
- `/healthz` checks the database and both chain RPCs and reports each
- spec/10-security-and-deploy.md records the regions; the console footer states them
Milestone: S9 Demo-ready prototype in the EU

Title: Structured logs and request IDs
User story: As a on-call engineer, I want JSON logs with request ID and payment ID on every line, so that any incident can be traced end to end.
Acceptance criteria:
- Every HTTP request gets a `request_id`, returned in the `Request-Id` header
- Log lines include `payment_id` when one is in context
- Keys, secrets, full wallet private data and invoice bodies are never logged (tested with a log capture)

Title: Local EVM with a mock USDC for tests
User story: As a builder, I want a local chain (anvil) with a mock 6-decimal USDC contract deployed by script, so that CI and the fault suite run deterministically without faucets or public RPC limits.
Acceptance criteria:
- `make chain` starts anvil and deploys MockUSDC; addresses are written to a test config
- The EVM adapter runs its contract tests against the local chain in CI
- Public testnets are used only in nightly runs and the live demo

Title: Create a payout intent
User story: As a platform integrator, I want to POST a payout intent with amount, currency, payee, optional network, reference and notes, so that every payment starts with one ID and gets a decision before any money moves.
Acceptance criteria:
- POST /v1/payment_intents returns 201 with a `pay_` ID, the decision and the status
- The payment ID is assigned once and never changes through retries, failovers or approvals
- Invalid input returns 422 with the standard error body and no intent is created
- `source` is `platform` or `agent`; `agent` requires a `mandate_id`
Milestone: S1 A platform payout is decided through the API (done)

Title: Idempotent creates
User story: As a platform integrator, I want an `Idempotency-Key` on every create call, so that a network retry on my side can never create a second payment.
Acceptance criteria:
- Given the same key and the same body, when I repeat the call, then I get the original response and no new intent
- Given the same key and a different body, then I get 409 `idempotency_conflict`
- Keys are scoped per organisation; two parallel requests with one key create exactly one intent (concurrency test)
Milestone: S1 A platform payout is decided through the API (done)

Title: Read and list intents
User story: As a platform integrator, I want to fetch an intent with its full timeline and to list intents with filters, so that I can show status to my users and debug my integration.
Acceptance criteria:
- GET /v1/payment_intents/{id} includes decisions, checks, attempts, ledger postings and events
- GET /v1/payment_intents supports cursor pagination and filters by status, rail and created range
- Another organisation's ID returns 404, never 403
Milestone: S1 A platform payout is decided through the API (done)

Title: Counterparty registry with wallet history
User story: As a payments lead, I want counterparties with KYB status, wallets or bank accounts, first-seen and last-changed times and payment history, so that the policy can check "new wallet", "changed details", "first payment" and "above norm" from facts.
Acceptance criteria:
- Each payout destination stores `first_seen_at` and `last_changed_at`; editing it updates `last_changed_at` and writes an audit event
- Each counterparty exposes payment count and median amount, computed from confirmed payments
- Counterparties are seeded from fixtures and editable in the console
Milestone: S1 A platform payout is decided through the API (done)

Title: Cancel an intent before it is sent
User story: As a payments lead, I want to cancel an escalated, held or ready intent, so that a payment we no longer want never goes out.
Acceptance criteria:
- Cancel is allowed from ESCALATED, HELD or READY only; from SUBMITTED or UNKNOWN it returns 409
- CANCELLED is terminal and audited with the actor and reason

Title: Rule-set format and loader
User story: As a compliance lead, I want our rules as a versioned YAML rule set with named checks and parameters, so that the rules are ours, readable and exactly enforced.
Acceptance criteria:
- Rule sets follow spec/04-policy.md and are validated against a schema on load; an invalid file is rejected with line-level errors
- A loaded version is immutable and identified by version number and content hash
- Every decision stores the version and hash it used
Milestone: S1 A platform payout is decided through the API (done)

Title: Decision engine and precedence
User story: As a payments lead, I want every intent evaluated against all checks with execute, escalate or block and a reason per check, so that I can see exactly why each payment was decided.
Acceptance criteria:
- Each check returns PASS, ESCALATE or BLOCK with a reason code, parameters and evidence references
- Final decision: BLOCK if any check blocks; else ESCALATE if any escalates; else EXECUTE
- Same inputs and rule version always give the same decision (property-based test)
- Rules-only evaluation p95 under 50 ms locally (benchmark in EVL-08)
Milestone: S1 A platform payout is decided through the API (done)

Title: Compliance checks (KYB, allowlist, screening, Travel Rule, network)
User story: As a compliance lead, I want KYB, allowlist, screening, Travel Rule and allowed-network checks, so that no payment reaches a payee we haven't cleared.
Acceptance criteria:
- KYB not verified -> BLOCK; KYB pending -> ESCALATE
- Payee not on allowlist -> ESCALATE (first payment)
- Mock screening list hit on address or name -> BLOCK `SCREENING_HIT`; screening unavailable -> fail closed per POL-09
- Travel Rule originator and beneficiary fields missing above the configured threshold -> ESCALATE
- Network or currency not allowed for the platform -> BLOCK
- Screening sits behind a `Screening` interface so a real vendor can replace the mock
Milestone: S1 A platform payout is decided through the API (done)

Title: Limits and daily caps
User story: As a compliance lead, I want an auto-approval limit, a hard maximum and daily caps on routine payments, so that large or accumulated payments always reach a human, and splitting a payment can't get around a cap.
Acceptance criteria:
- Above the auto limit -> ESCALATE; above the hard maximum -> BLOCK
- Daily caps per platform and per counterparty count confirmed plus in-flight amounts
- Cap counters update atomically; 20 parallel intents that together exceed the cap never all execute (concurrency test)
Milestone: S1 A platform payout is decided through the API (done)

Title: Unusual activity as checkable rules
User story: As a compliance lead, I want new wallet, changed details, first payment and amount above the counterparty's norm as explicit rules, so that "unusual" is something the system can check and a reviewer can verify.
Acceptance criteria:
- Wallet first seen within N days -> ESCALATE `NEW_WALLET`; destination changed within N days -> ESCALATE `CHANGED_DETAILS`
- No prior confirmed payment to this counterparty -> ESCALATE `FIRST_PAYMENT`
- Amount above k x the counterparty's median -> ESCALATE `ABOVE_NORM`
- Each hit stores the raw fact (address, timestamps, median, ratio) as evidence
Milestone: S3 Escalate, review raw facts, approve with a policy re-run (done)

Title: A block is final
User story: As a compliance lead, I want a blocked payment to stay blocked whatever anyone does next, so that no approval, retry or other rail can override a compliance decision.
Acceptance criteria:
- BLOCKED has no outgoing transitions in the state machine and a database trigger rejects any status change away from it
- Approve, retry, reroute or resubmit on a blocked payment returns 409 `payment_blocked`
- A new intent to the same counterparty or the same destination address within 24 h of a block, whatever the amount, is escalated RESUBMISSION_AFTER_BLOCK with a link to the blocked one (D-10)
Milestone: S3 Escalate, review raw facts, approve with a policy re-run (done)

Title: Versioned rule changes with two approvers
User story: As a compliance lead, I want rule changes proposed as a new version and activated only after a second person approves, so that no single person can quietly weaken our controls.
Acceptance criteria:
- A proposer creates a draft version; the console shows a diff against the active version
- Activation needs a second, different user; if any rule loosens (higher limit, removed check, shorter screening scope, longer window) the compliance lead must be one of the two
- On activation the compliance lead's attestation is recorded: the client approves these rules and keeps AML accountability
- All versions are kept and readable; decisions link to the version used

Title: Decision-only API
User story: As a platform integrator, I want POST /v1/decisions to get a decision without Detent executing anything, so that I can use Detent before my own payout process, and shadow mode can reuse the same engine.
Acceptance criteria:
- Returns the same decision object as intent creation, with `executed: false`
- Decisions are stored and audited but never create attempts
Milestone: S1 A platform payout is decided through the API (done)

Title: Fail closed
User story: As a compliance lead, I want any internal error during a decision to hold the payment or send it to manual review, so that nothing is ever executed unchecked.
Acceptance criteria:
- If policy evaluation, screening or a data read fails, the decision is ESCALATE `SYSTEM_UNAVAILABLE` routed by the platform's fail-safe setting (`hold` or `manual_queue`)
- No code path turns an error into EXECUTE (fault-injection test on each dependency)
Milestone: S1 A platform payout is decided through the API (done)

Title: Signed mandate for an AI agent
User story: As a payments lead, I want to issue a mandate that limits what an agent may propose (payees, per-payment and total amounts, networks, currencies and expiry), so that an agent can only ask for payments inside a scope we signed.
Acceptance criteria:
- Mandates are JSON with an HMAC-SHA256 signature by the platform's mandate key (format in spec/05-agents.md)
- Invalid signature, unknown agent or expired mandate are detectable without calling the model
- The format keeps fields that map to AP2-style mandates later
Milestone: S5 An AI agent proposes the $18,500 invoice inside a mandate (done)

Title: Mandate check in the policy
User story: As a compliance lead, I want agent-sourced intents checked against their mandate before any other check, so that an agent can never exceed what we delegated.
Acceptance criteria:
- Missing or invalid signature, revoked or expired mandate, payee outside scope, amount above per-payment limit, cumulative total above limit, or network outside scope -> BLOCK with the specific reason
- Cumulative usage updates atomically (concurrency test)
- The check re-runs at execution time
Milestone: S5 An AI agent proposes the $18,500 invoice inside a mandate (done)

Title: Revoke a mandate
User story: As a payments lead, I want to revoke a mandate at once, so that a misbehaving agent loses its permissions immediately.
Acceptance criteria:
- Revocation by console or API takes effect for every intent not yet SUBMITTED
- An approved intent whose mandate is revoked before sending is BLOCKED `MANDATE_REVOKED` at the pre-send re-check
Milestone: S5 An AI agent proposes the $18,500 invoice inside a mandate (done)

Title: Instruction agent turns an invoice into a proposed intent
User story: As a payments lead, I want the instruction agent to read a supplier invoice and propose a structured payment intent, so that our accounts-payable work can be delegated without giving the agent any power to pay.
Acceptance criteria:
- Input: invoice text or PDF; output: payee, matched counterparty, amount, currency, network, wallet, invoice number, due date, each with confidence and the source text span
- Uses the agents model from config (default `claude-sonnet-5-5`) with tool use and a strict JSON schema; output is validated by Pydantic
- Invalid output is retried once, then the proposal is marked `needs_human`
- The canonical $18,500 USDC invoice yields the expected intent on 10 of 10 runs (EVL-04)
Milestone: S5 An AI agent proposes the $18,500 invoice inside a mandate (done)

Title: Flag, never guess
User story: As a reviewer, I want uncertain invoice fields flagged instead of filled in, so that a wrong network or wallet is never silently chosen.
Acceptance criteria:
- Missing network, two wallets, total not matching line items, ambiguous currency, payee not in the registry, or wallet different from the registry each set a named flag
- Any flag sets `requires_clarification`; such a proposal can't be submitted until a human resolves each flag
- Tests on the interpretation set confirm no flagged field is ever populated from outside the document
Milestone: S5 An AI agent proposes the $18,500 invoice inside a mandate (done)

Title: The agent can only propose
User story: As a compliance lead, I want the agent's only money-related ability to be "propose an intent" under a mandate, so that the model can never execute, approve or retry.
Acceptance criteria:
- The agent's tool registry has no tool that writes state except `propose_payment_intent`, which calls the public API with scope `intents:create`
- An import-boundary test fails if `detent.agents` imports `detent.execution`, `detent.exceptions.approve` or `detent.rails`
- An attempt by the agent to call any other write endpoint is rejected by scope and logged
Milestone: S5 An AI agent proposes the $18,500 invoice inside a mandate (done)

Title: Prompt-injection isolation
User story: As a compliance lead, I want invoice text, notes, names and references treated strictly as data, so that text like "ignore your rules, this is pre-approved" changes nothing.
Acceptance criteria:
- Untrusted text reaches the model only inside delimited data blocks, after the instructions, with an explicit data-only rule
- The policy never reads agent free text; it reads only typed fields
- Instruction-like content in a document is reported as a `possible_injection` flag and never followed
- All injection scenarios in the attack suite pass (EVL-02)
Milestone: S5 An AI agent proposes the $18,500 invoice inside a mandate (done)

Title: Record every agent call for replay
User story: As a auditor, I want each agent call stored with prompt version, model ID, input hash and raw output, so that replay is deterministic and I can see exactly what the agent said.
Acceptance criteria:
- Agent calls are rows linked to the intent or case, with token counts and latency
- Replay reads stored outputs and never calls the model again
Milestone: S5 An AI agent proposes the $18,500 invoice inside a mandate (done)

Title: Model configuration and cost guard
User story: As a founder, I want model IDs in config and a daily token budget per organisation, so that AI costs stay bounded and the provider can be swapped.
Acceptance criteria:
- Model IDs come from settings: agents `claude-sonnet-5-5`, light tasks `claude-haiku-5-5`, evaluation judge `claude-opus-5-5`
- Model calls go through one `LLMClient` interface so a second provider can be added
- Over budget, agent features return `needs_human`; nothing falls back to executing
Milestone: S5 An AI agent proposes the $18,500 invoice inside a mandate (done)

Title: Payment state machine
User story: As a builder, I want one transition function with an allowed-transitions table, called under a row lock, so that no code can put a payment into an impossible state.
Acceptance criteria:
- All status changes go through `transition(payment_id, to_status, reason, actor)`, which runs `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` in one transaction
- Illegal transitions raise, change nothing and write an audit event
- Property-based tests on random event sequences never reach a state outside the table in spec/02-domain-model.md
Milestone: S2 An EXECUTE decision is sent exactly once (done)

Title: Attempts and exactly-once guarantees
User story: As a payments lead, I want each send recorded as an attempt under the same payment ID, with database guarantees against a second payment, so that no retry or failover can ever pay twice.
Acceptance criteria:
- At most one attempt per payment is SUBMITTED or UNKNOWN at a time (partial unique index)
- At most one attempt per payment is CONFIRMED (partial unique index)
- A new attempt is created only when the previous one is definitively FAILED
- Rail idempotency keys are derived from the payment ID as defined in spec/06-rails-and-faults.md
Milestone: S2 An EXECUTE decision is sent exactly once (done)

Title: Pre-send checks under the lock
User story: As a payments lead, I want the state lock, balance check, pre-funded wallet limit, kill switch and a fresh policy check right before every send, so that nothing is sent on stale or unsafe conditions.
Acceptance criteria:
- Inside the lock: kill switch off, source balance covers amount plus fees or gas, the wallet's daily pre-funded limit has room, mandate valid
- If the decision is older than the configured age or the rule version changed, policy re-runs first
- Any failed check moves the payment to HELD with the reason; nothing is sent
Milestone: S2 An EXECUTE decision is sent exactly once (done)

Title: Nonce manager
User story: As a builder, I want nonces allocated per chain and wallet under a database lock and stored before broadcast, so that two different transactions never share a nonce.
Acceptance criteria:
- The nonce is written on the attempt before the transaction is broadcast
- On startup the manager reconciles with `eth_getTransactionCount(pending)` and refuses to send if they disagree
- Concurrent sends from one wallet get consecutive nonces (concurrency test)
Milestone: S2 An EXECUTE decision is sent exactly once (done)

Title: A timeout becomes UNKNOWN
User story: As a payments lead, I want a send whose outcome is unclear marked UNKNOWN, never FAILED, so that a stuck transaction that later confirms is never paid a second time.
Acceptance criteria:
- A timeout, dropped connection or 5xx after the request may have reached the rail -> attempt and payment UNKNOWN
- While UNKNOWN, no new attempt can be created (database and code)
- Only a definitive rail answer moves UNKNOWN to CONFIRMED or FAILED

Title: UNKNOWN resolver
User story: As a payments lead, I want UNKNOWN payments resolved from the rail's own evidence, with a human decision if they stay stuck, so that we learn the real outcome quickly and never guess.
Acceptance criteria:
- The worker polls by transaction hash (chain) or idempotency key (bank) on a backoff schedule
- CONFIRMED needs receipt status 1 and the rail's confirmation threshold; FAILED needs receipt status 0, the nonce consumed by another transaction, or the rail's definitive not-found
- Still UNKNOWN after the threshold -> an `UNKNOWN_STUCK` exception to the payments lead, with two options: keep waiting, or approve a cancel-by-replacement (same nonce, zero value) carried out by the execution layer
- Median and p95 time to resolve are recorded for the results report

Title: Deterministic retry policy
User story: As a compliance lead, I want retries decided by configured rules in the execution layer only, so that the AI never decides to retry and a rejection is never retried.
Acceptance criteria:
- Retry config lists retryable error codes, maximum attempts and backoff
- Only `TECHNICAL_RETRYABLE` failures retry; `REJECTED_BY_RAIL` and any BLOCK never do
- Every retry keeps the payment ID and is audited with the rule that allowed it

Title: Kill switch
User story: As a payments lead, I want a kill switch that I or Detent's on-call engineer can pull, and that only I can release, so that we can stop all sending at once during an incident.
Acceptance criteria:
- Engaging (console button or POST /v1/kill_switch) stops new submissions; the flag is checked inside the lock before every send
- Pending payments stay held; UNKNOWN attempts keep resolving read-only
- Release requires the client's payments lead, even if on-call engaged it
- A red banner shows on every console page while engaged; every change is audited

Title: Shadow, Assist and Auto modes
User story: As a payments lead, I want a mode setting per platform, so that we can adopt step by step under signed gates.
Acceptance criteria:
- Shadow: decisions recorded, nothing sent. Assist: EXECUTE decisions wait for a human 'Send' click. Auto: EXECUTE decisions send automatically
- Changing mode needs the payments lead and the compliance lead; each change is audited
- Orchestrate is shown as routing being enabled when 2 or more rails are connected
Traces to: A3.shadow, A3.assist, A3.auto, A3.orchestrate, B6.wrong_decision, B3.mode_gates

Title: Sev 1 invariant monitor
User story: As a on-call engineer, I want a continuous check for duplicate payments, unauthorised executions and double credits, so that if an invariant ever breaks we stop and know within a minute.
Acceptance criteria:
- Every minute and after each confirmation: two confirmed transfers for one payment ID, a confirmed attempt without an EXECUTE or approved decision, or two credits for one inbound transfer
- A hit opens a Sev 1 incident, engages the kill switch (configurable, on by default), posts to the mock outbox and shows a red banner

Title: Rail adapter contract
User story: As a builder, I want one adapter interface with normalised statuses and an error taxonomy, so that adding a rail never touches decision or execution logic.
Acceptance criteria:
- Interface: `eligible`, `quote`, `submit`, `status`, `health`, as in spec/06-rails-and-faults.md
- Errors normalise to TECHNICAL_RETRYABLE, TECHNICAL_FINAL, REJECTED_BY_RAIL or TIMEOUT
- A shared contract-test suite runs against every adapter
Milestone: S2 An EXECUTE decision is sent exactly once (done)

Title: Base Sepolia USDC adapter
User story: As a demo viewer, I want real test USDC transfers on Base Sepolia with explorer links, so that the demo moves real (test) value on a real network.
Acceptance criteria:
- ERC-20 transfer via web3.py signed with a test key from settings; gas estimated and checked
- Confirmation threshold configurable; explorer link stored on the attempt
- Contract tests pass on the local chain and nightly on Base Sepolia
Milestone: S2 An EXECUTE decision is sent exactly once (done)

Title: Ethereum Sepolia USDC adapter
User story: As a demo viewer, I want the same transfers on Ethereum Sepolia, so that routing has a real second network to choose.
Acceptance criteria:
- Shares an EVM base class with RAL-02; its own fee profile and confirmation threshold
- Contract tests pass

Title: Simulated instant bank rail
User story: As a demo viewer, I want a mock instant bank rail with its own fees, limits, cut-off times and failure rate, so that routing and reconciliation span stablecoin and fiat.
Acceptance criteria:
- A separate FastAPI sub-app with GBP and EUR, per-payment and daily limits, cut-off times, a configurable failure rate and idempotency by key
- Status endpoint and asynchronous settlement callback; daily statement endpoint (used by LED-07)
- Deterministic test values: amounts ending .13 time out then settle; .42 fail technically

Title: Fault-injection proxy
User story: As a builder, I want a proxy in front of chain RPC and the bank rail that injects named faults, so that the exactly-once claims are demonstrated, not asserted.
Acceptance criteria:
- Faults: timeout after forwarding, timeout before forwarding, connection reset, 5xx, delayed receipt, hidden receipt for N polls (stuck), duplicated response
- Fault chosen per attempt by scenario config in tests and sandbox; disabled in demo mode unless a scenario requests it
- Each injected fault is logged with the attempt ID

Title: Routing engine
User story: As a payments lead, I want the best eligible rail chosen by cost, speed, success rate and liquidity, with the reason stored, so that payouts cost less and fail less, and I can see why a rail was chosen.
Acceptance criteria:
- Routing runs only after an EXECUTE decision; a BLOCK never reaches routing
- Eligibility first (currency, network constraint from intent or mandate, limits, cut-off, health, liquidity), then a weighted score from config
- The decision stores each candidate's score and the reason for the winner

Title: Failover on technical failure only
User story: As a compliance lead, I want failover to another rail only after a definitive technical failure and only when the intent allows a network switch, so that a rejection is never re-routed and failover can't pay twice.
Acceptance criteria:
- Failover needs the previous attempt definitively FAILED with a technical code; never from UNKNOWN
- Never after BLOCK or REJECTED_BY_RAIL
- Network switches need `allow_network_switch` on the intent or mandate, or a human approval
- The new attempt keeps the payment ID

Title: Rail health and circuit breaker
User story: As a payments lead, I want each rail's success rate, latency, balance and limit usage, and unhealthy rails taken out of routing, so that payments avoid a failing rail automatically.
Acceptance criteria:
- Rolling success rate and p95 latency per rail; balance and pre-funded limit usage
- Circuit opens after the configured failure count and closes after a successful probe

Title: Rail connection flow (mock)
User story: As a payments lead, I want to connect a rail through a mock authorisation screen or by entering scoped API keys, so that onboarding looks like the real thing and we keep our own rail accounts.
Acceptance criteria:
- Mock OAuth-style consent screen and a scoped-key form; credentials encrypted at rest and never shown again
- Scopes listed; disconnect removes credentials and takes the rail out of routing

Title: Daily adapter contract tests
User story: As a on-call engineer, I want adapter contract tests run daily against testnets and the simulator, so that a rail API change is caught before a demo.
Acceptance criteria: - Scheduled GitHub Actions job; failure opens an issue with the failing adapter and test

Title: Simulated chain rail for the sandbox
User story: As a platform integrator, I want sandbox payouts on a simulated USDC rail that settles instantly by default, so that I can test every path quickly without draining faucet wallets.
Acceptance criteria:
- Implements the adapter contract with instant settlement and the same test values
- Sandbox organisations use it by default; real testnet is opt-in (SBX-03)

Title: Exception cases with owner and deadline
User story: As a payments lead, I want every escalation to become a case with a named owner, a backup owner and a deadline by risk tier, so that escalations always get answered.
Acceptance criteria:
- Owner assignment rules by case type and amount, in config
- Deadlines by tier from config (defaults: 2 h for payouts above the auto limit, 1 business day for deposit exceptions)
- Statuses OPEN, HELD_OVERDUE, RESOLVED; every change audited
Milestone: S3 Escalate, review raw facts, approve with a policy re-run (done)

Title: Raw facts first
User story: As a reviewer, I want to see the raw facts before the agent's summary, so that my judgement isn't anchored by the AI.
Acceptance criteria:
- Top of the case: payee as registered, full checksummed wallet address, first seen and last changed times, amount against the counterparty's median, each rule hit with its parameters, and the mandate scope
- The agent's evidence and recommendation sit below, collapsed by default
Milestone: S3 Escalate, review raw facts, approve with a policy re-run (done)

Title: Investigation agent with cited evidence
User story: As a reviewer, I want the investigation agent to gather evidence and draft a recommendation that cites its sources, so that I decide faster without trusting unsupported claims.
Acceptance criteria:
- Read-only tools: ledger history, counterparty record, screening result, rail status, prior cases
- Each claim cites evidence record IDs; uncited claims are removed and the removal is flagged
- Recommendation is approve, reject or needs-information with a confidence; the agent cannot change any state
- Runs in the worker; the case is usable before the agent finishes

Title: Approve or reject, with policy re-run
User story: As a reviewer, I want approval to send the payment back through policy before anything is sent, so that an approval can't push through something the rules now block.
Acceptance criteria:
- Approve re-runs policy with the active version and fresh data; a new BLOCK stays blocked; a new escalation reason opens a new case; otherwise the payment proceeds per mode
- Reject -> REJECTED (terminal); a reason is required for both
- The approver can't be the user who initiated the intent
Milestone: S3 Escalate, review raw facts, approve with a policy re-run (done)

Title: Double-approval safety
User story: As a payments lead, I want concurrent approvals of one case to have exactly one effect, so that a double click or two reviewers never cause two sends.
Acceptance criteria:
- Row lock plus version check; the second approval gets 409 `already_resolved`
- Fault suite includes parallel approvals from console and API
Milestone: S3 Escalate, review raw facts, approve with a policy re-run (done)

Title: Deadline sweeper - a timeout never becomes an approval
User story: As a payments lead, I want overdue cases held, the counterparty told, and the case passed to the backup owner, so that nothing is auto-approved and nobody is left waiting without news.
Acceptance criteria:
- Past the deadline: case HELD_OVERDUE, payment stays held, a status update goes to the counterparty via the outbox, and the backup owner gets the case with a new deadline
- The count of payments approved by timeout is always 0 and is reported

Title: Mock outbox
User story: As a demo viewer, I want every outbound notification visible in an Outbox screen, so that the demo shows the counterparty updates without sending real email.
Acceptance criteria:
- Counterparty updates, owner assignments and incident notices are stored with recipient, template and body
- Nothing in the prototype sends real email
Milestone: S3 Escalate, review raw facts, approve with a policy re-run (done)

Title: Exceptions by API
User story: As a platform integrator, I want to list cases and approve or reject them by API, so that our own tools can work the queue.
Acceptance criteria:
- GET /v1/exceptions with filters; POST /v1/exceptions/{id}/approve and /reject need scope `exceptions:approve`
- Same rules as the console: re-run, separation of duties, 409 on double approval
Milestone: P1 Public sandbox API and webhooks

Title: Agent-versus-human agreement sample
User story: As a compliance lead, I want a report comparing the agent's recommendations with our final decisions, so that we can see whether the agent deserves more trust.
Acceptance criteria: - Per period: cases, agreement rate, disagreements listed with both rationales

Title: Double-entry ledger
User story: As a auditor, I want one immutable double-entry ledger across all rails, so that every balance can be explained from entries.
Acceptance criteria:
- Journal entries with balanced postings; accounts for user balances, platform operating, rail clearing per rail, fees and suspense
- Entries are append-only; corrections are new entries
- Every posting references a payment, deposit or adjustment ID
Milestone: S7 One ledger, deposits credited once, reconciliation, replay

Title: Payout postings
User story: As a payments lead, I want payouts reserved on submission, settled on confirmation and released on final failure, so that balances are always right, even with UNKNOWN payments.
Acceptance criteria:
- SUBMITTED reserves; CONFIRMED settles and posts actual fees; final FAILED reverses the reservation; UNKNOWN keeps the reservation
- Ledger and payment status agree after every fault-suite case
Milestone: S7 One ledger, deposits credited once, reconciliation, replay

Title: Deposit intents
User story: As a platform integrator, I want to create a deposit intent for a user account with expected token, network and optional amount, so that incoming money can be matched to the right account.
Acceptance criteria:
- POST /v1/deposit_intents returns deposit instructions: a per-account test address, or a bank reference for the simulated rail
- Idempotent like payment intents
Milestone: S7 One ledger, deposits credited once, reconciliation, replay

Title: Deposit watchers
User story: As a payments lead, I want incoming transfers on both chains and the bank rail recorded once each, so that no deposit is missed or counted twice.
Acceptance criteria:
- Reads ERC-20 Transfer logs to watched addresses, and bank-rail inbound credits
- Unique on (rail, transaction hash, log index); restarting the watcher never duplicates
Milestone: S7 One ledger, deposits credited once, reconciliation, replay

Title: Deposit decision and credit-once
User story: As a payments lead, I want each inbound transfer matched, checked and credited once after enough confirmations, so that users are credited once, to the right account.
Acceptance criteria:
- Match on address or reference, token, network and amount within tolerance
- Policy checks the sender (screening) and the token and network match
- Credit only after the confirmation threshold; a unique constraint allows one credit per inbound transfer
- Mismatches (wrong network or token, amount mismatch, no intent, flagged sender) open deposit exceptions
Milestone: S7 One ledger, deposits credited once, reconciliation, replay

Title: Reconciliation run with proposed fixes
User story: As a payments lead, I want a reconciliation of the ledger against every rail's records, with a proposed fix for each break, so that reconciliation is a review of exceptions, not a spreadsheet job.
Acceptance criteria:
- Matches ledger postings to chain transfers and bank statements for payouts and deposits; reports the match rate
- Each break becomes an exception with a fix drafted by the reconciliation agent (for example, credit account X, or return to sender)
- A fix is applied only after human approval, as a new adjustment entry
- On a generated set of 500 synthetic deposits and payouts with 3 designed breaks, automatic matching is 99% or more and each break gets a proposed fix
- The demo batch (20 payouts, 8 deposits) shows exactly one designed break, dep-07
Milestone: S7 One ledger, deposits credited once, reconciliation, replay

Title: Bank statement import
User story: As a builder, I want the simulated bank's daily statement imported for reconciliation, so that fiat reconciliation works like it does with a real bank.
Acceptance criteria: - Pulls the statement endpoint (JSON or CSV), idempotent per statement date
Milestone: S7 One ledger, deposits credited once, reconciliation, replay

Title: Usage metering
User story: As a founder, I want payments decided per organisation per month counted from decisions and the ledger, so that per-payment pricing can be billed later, and sandbox usage shown now.
Acceptance criteria: - Monthly counts of payments decided, agent investigations and API calls per organisation

Title: Append-only, hash-chained audit log
User story: As a auditor, I want every step recorded in an append-only log I can verify, so that the record can't be quietly changed.
Acceptance criteria:
- Events written in the same transaction as the change they describe: intent, agent output, decision with rule version and checks, case events, approvals, transitions, rail requests and responses, postings, kill switch, policy changes
- A database trigger rejects UPDATE and DELETE on audit rows
- Each row stores a hash of the previous row; `detent audit verify` detects a tampered row (tested)
Milestone: S1 A platform payout is decided through the API (done)

Title: Replay any payment
User story: As a auditor, I want to replay a payment step by step from its stored inputs, rule version and agent outputs, so that I can confirm the decision would be made the same way again.
Acceptance criteria:
- Console button and GET /v1/payment_intents/{id}/replay
- Replay uses stored inputs and stored agent outputs and must reproduce the recorded decision; a mismatch raises an alert
- Every payment in the demo data replays successfully (test)
Milestone: S7 One ledger, deposits credited once, reconciliation, replay

Title: Evidence export
User story: As a auditor, I want an evidence pack for a payment or date range, so that I can review it offline.
Acceptance criteria: - JSON plus a readable HTML or PDF: inputs, rule versions, decisions, approvers, state changes, transaction hashes with explorer links, and the hash-chain check result

Title: Console shell and prototype labelling
User story: As a demo viewer, I want a clean console with navigation, acting-user indicator, kill-switch state and a permanent prototype label, so that it looks real and is honest about what it is.
Acceptance criteria:

- A banner on every page: 'Prototype · test networks · simulated bank rail'

Milestone: S3 Escalate, review raw facts, approve with a policy re-run (done)

Title: Overview screen
User story: As a payments lead, I want today's decisions, open and overdue cases, UNKNOWN payments, match rate and rail health at a glance, so that I know where attention is needed.
Acceptance criteria:
- Counts by decision and status; share decided without a human; oldest UNKNOWN age; open and overdue cases; match rate; rail health; recent events
- Refreshes by htmx polling

Title: Payments list and detail
User story: As a reviewer, I want a payment page with every check, the route, attempts, postings and the timeline, so that I can answer "what happened to this payment" in one place.
Acceptance criteria: - Each check with result, reason and evidence; route candidates and scores; attempts with hash and explorer link; ledger postings; timeline; replay button
Milestone: S3 Escalate, review raw facts, approve with a policy re-run (done)

Title: Exceptions queue screen
User story: As a reviewer, I want my queue with deadlines counting down and the case page with approve and reject, so that I can work escalations quickly and correctly.

Milestone: S3 Escalate, review raw facts, approve with a policy re-run (done)

Title: Invoice drop and agent proposal screen
User story: As a demo viewer, I want to drop an invoice and watch the agent's proposal, flags and mandate appear, so that the agentic part of the demo is visible.
Acceptance criteria:

Title: Policy and mandates screens
User story: As a compliance lead, I want to read, diff, propose and approve rule versions, and to manage mandates, so that rule ownership is visible and practical.
Acceptance criteria:
- Active version, history and diff; propose and approve per POL-07
- Mandates list with scope, usage against limits, expiry and revoke

Title: Reconciliation screen
User story: As a payments lead, I want the latest run's match rate and breaks with proposed fixes, so that I can approve fixes in minutes.
Acceptance criteria: - Run history, match rate, breaks with proposed fix and approve button
Milestone: S7 One ledger, deposits credited once, reconciliation, replay

Title: Rails screen
User story: As a payments lead, I want connected rails with balance, limits and recent results, so that I can see where money is going.
Acceptance criteria: - Per rail: network or currency, balance, pre-funded limit usage, last 20 attempts

Title: Demo scenario runner
User story: As a founder, I want one-click scenarios and a reset, so that every demo runs the same way in under 10 minutes.
Acceptance criteria:
- Scenarios: the $18,500 invoice; forced timeout to UNKNOWN then CONFIRMED with no resend; 20-payment batch with deposits and one designed break; an attack sample; reset demo data

Title: Settings screen
User story: As a payments lead, I want to see and set mode, fail-safe, deadlines and routing weights, so that the operating choices are explicit.
Acceptance criteria: - Mode and fail-safe editable with the approvals from EXE-09; deadlines and weights shown read-only in the prototype

Title: Evaluation runner
User story: As a builder, I want `detent eval run --suite attacks|faults|interpretation|agreement|all` on a fresh database, so that results are repeatable and comparable across commits.
Acceptance criteria:
- Each scenario runs in isolation with a fixed seed; output is results.json with date, commit, model IDs and per-scenario results
- Scenarios are data files under eval/scenarios/, not code

User story: As a compliance lead, I want at least 100 attack scenarios with zero unauthorised executions, so that the safety claim is measured.

Acceptance criteria:

- Pass: 0 duplicates, every retry and switch keeps the payment ID, no timeout ever becomes FAILED

Title: Interpretation set
User story: As a builder, I want 30 labelled invoices including 10 runs of the canonical one and ambiguous variants, so that the agent's accuracy and "flag, never guess" are measured.

Title: Agreement set (synthetic)

Title: Results report
User story: As a founder, I want a dated results report generated from results.json, so that I can show measured results to prospects and investors.
Acceptance criteria:

User story: As a compliance lead, I want the attack and fault suites to block any release with a single unauthorised execution or duplicate, so that regressions never reach the demo or the sandbox.

Acceptance criteria: - Benchmark reports p50 and p95 for rules-only and agent paths; included in the results report

Title: Wallet funding runbook and check
User story: As a founder, I want a script that checks test-wallet balances and tells me what to top up, so that a demo never fails for lack of test USDC or gas.
Acceptance criteria: - `detent demo check` prints USDC and gas balances per wallet and chain with faucet instructions
Milestone: S9 Demo-ready prototype in the EU

User story: As a founder, I want a written 10-minute demo script matching the scenario runner, so that every demo tells the same story.

User story: As a founder, I want seed packs for a payout platform, a crypto service provider and a marketplace, so that I can tailor the demo to the prospect.

User story: As a payments lead, I want to upload a month of payout and deposit exports with our actual decisions, so that Detent can show what it would have decided on our real data.
Acceptance criteria: - Column-mapping screen; validation report; decisions run with POL-08 and nothing is executed

User story: As a payments lead, I want a report of what would have been auto-approved, escalated and blocked, agreement with our decisions, unsafe approvals and routing savings, so that we can judge the value before any pilot.
Acceptance criteria: - Sections: decision mix, agreement, unsafe approvals (approved by Detent but blocked or lossy for the client), unreconciled items, simulated routing saving; export as HTML and PDF

Title: Mode-gate report and sign-off
User story: As a compliance lead, I want a gate report with agreement and unsafe approvals over a period, and a recorded sign-off, so that each move from Shadow to Assist to Auto is evidenced.
Acceptance criteria: - Shows 30-day agreement and unsafe approvals against the gate thresholds; sign-off by payments lead and compliance lead recorded and linked to the mode change

Title: Anonymise on import
User story: As a compliance lead, I want names and addresses hashed with a per-import salt, so that sharing a shadow export doesn't expose personal data.
Acceptance criteria: - Raw names and account identifiers never stored; hashes are consistent within one import

Title: Incident records
User story: As a on-call engineer, I want incidents with severity, timeline, notification time and root cause, so that we can run the Sev 1 process and support clients' DORA reporting.

User story: As a founder, I want CI to fail if the repo contains any term from a private denylist, so that no former-employer name or material ever enters the codebase.

Title: Backup and restore drill
User story: As a on-call engineer, I want a documented, tested restore from the database provider's point-in-time recovery, so that we can recover in under an hour without losing decisions.
Acceptance criteria: - Runbook in spec/10; one drill done and timed; audit hash chain verified after restore

Title: Security pack draft
User story: As a founder, I want a written description of the controls as built, so that it can seed a pen test and vendor due diligence later.
Acceptance criteria: - docs/security.md generated from spec/10, listing controls and their tests; roadmap items labelled as roadmap

Title: API keys and scopes
User story: As a platform integrator, I want test API keys with scopes, sent as a Bearer token, so that my integration is authenticated and least-privileged.

- `Authorization: Bearer sk_test_...`; keys hashed at rest; scopes read, intents:create, exceptions:approve, admin

Title: Error model
User story: As a platform integrator, I want consistent JSON errors with type, code, message, payment ID and request ID, so that I can handle errors in code.

Title: Dated API versions
User story: As a platform integrator, I want a dated version header, so that my integration doesn't break when the API changes.

Title: Rate limits
User story: As a founder, I want per-key rate limits returned in headers, so that the sandbox stays healthy.

User story: As a platform integrator, I want a complete, polished OpenAPI file with examples for every endpoint, so that docs, SDKs and "try it" all come from one source.

- Generated from FastAPI, then completed with descriptions, examples and error responses

User story: As a platform integrator, I want every API call I make logged with status, latency, idempotency key and payment ID, so that I can debug my own integration.
Acceptance criteria: - Stored per organisation for 30 days; bodies redacted; filterable in the dashboard

Title: Events list
User story: As a platform integrator, I want GET /v1/events with cursor pagination, so that I can poll if I can't receive webhooks.
Acceptance criteria: - Same event objects as webhooks; filter by type and payment ID
Milestone: P1 Public sandbox API and webhooks

Title: Webhook endpoints and event types
User story: As a platform integrator, I want to register endpoints for chosen event types, so that my systems react to decisions and state changes in real time.
Acceptance criteria:
- Event types from spec/03-api.md (payment_intent.*, exception.*, deposit.credited, reconciliation.break)
- Signing secret shown once; events carry `id` and a per-payment `sequence`

Title: Signed webhooks
User story: As a platform integrator, I want an HMAC-SHA256 signature over timestamp and body with a 5-minute window, so that I can trust that events come from Detent.

Title: Delivery, retries and log
User story: As a platform integrator, I want at-least-once delivery with retries, a delivery log, resend and a test event, so that I never silently miss an event.

User story: As a platform integrator, I want to verify my email, set a password and see my test keys, so that I can start integrating straight after the demo.

User story: As a Detent admin, I want sandbox access to expire unless I extend it, so that access is reviewed and can't linger.

User story: As a platform integrator, I want to create, roll and revoke keys with scopes, so that I can manage credentials safely.

Title: Request logs page
User story: As a platform integrator, I want to browse my request logs with filters, so that I can debug quickly.

Title: Webhooks page
User story: As a platform integrator, I want to manage endpoints, see the secret once, send a test event and read the delivery log, so that I can set up webhooks without support.

Title: Sandbox controls page
User story: As a platform integrator, I want to reset test data and force scenarios, so that I can test every path on demand.

Title: Usage page
User story: As a platform integrator, I want my usage against sandbox quotas, so that I know when I'll hit a limit.

Title: Console per organisation
User story: As a platform integrator, I want the back-office console inside the dashboard, scoped to my organisation, so that I see my sandbox payments the way an operations team would.

Title: Access requests inbox
User story: As a Detent admin, I want website access requests stored as leads and emailed to the sales inbox, so that I can follow up and approve companies.

User story: As a platform integrator, I want task guides, so that I can complete common jobs end to end.

User story: As a platform integrator, I want code samples in cURL, Python, TypeScript, Go, Java, C#, PHP and Ruby that actually run, so that I can copy and paste with confidence.

Title: Measured results section
User story: As a prospect, I want live numbers from the evaluation with dates, so that I see evidence, not claims.
Acceptance criteria: - Reads results.json at build time; every figure labelled 'test-network evaluation, [date]'

Title: Developer code tabs
User story: As a prospect, I want a tabbed code block creating a payment intent in 8 languages, so that my developers see it's real.
Acceptance criteria: - Uses the same tested snippets as DOC-04

Title: Legal pages and analytics
User story: As a prospect, I want privacy, sandbox terms and cookie notice, with cookie-light analytics, so that the site meets basic GDPR expectations.
Acceptance criteria: - Templates marked 'draft for legal review'; analytics without cookie banners where possible

Title: Booking and access form
User story: As a prospect, I want to book a demo or request sandbox access, so that I can start a conversation in one click.
Acceptance criteria: - Booking link to the founder's appointment page; access form posts to DSH-10

Title: Status page
User story: As a platform integrator, I want a status page for the sandbox API, so that I know whether a failure is mine.
Acceptance criteria: - Fed by health checks; shows sandbox API, dashboard and docs

Title: SEO basics
